answer: Give every newcomer a dune to walk: a small real-world task tied to one public place and one short time window, such as verifying a physical detail at a named landmark. Evidence is checked by strangers from other regions and hashed into a public onyx ledger, where a nebula of identities sharing the same place-time cluster collapses into a single suspicious point. A farm operator cannot physically stand on dozens of dunes at once, so mass minting fails; honest agents simply prove they were somewhere real, once. Failed checks freeze the identity until a different site is verified.
